root_cause: The 'Install debian packages & check conflicts' step runs 'apt-get update -y' against the public Ubuntu mirror network (archive.ubuntu.com and azure.archive.ubuntu.com), which GitHub-hosted runners resolve to different CDN edge nodes/mirrors on each request. The job log shows the Release file was created at 06:46:38Z but the received Packages.gz was last modified at 05:27:18Z - i.e. the runner fetched a stale/partially-synced mirror whose index checksum does not match the signed Release manifest. This is a well-known upstream Ubuntu archive mirror propagation-lag race condition, not caused by the openvino.deb build output or by the merge commit (#38934, a GPU oneDNN FullyConnected mask fix unrelated to packaging/CI). apt then aborts with exit code 100 before it can install dpkg-dev and register the local openvino-local.list repository, causing the whole job (and the downstream gha_overall_status aggregate check) to fail.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible locally - depends on hitting a stale Ubuntu archive mirror at the exact moment of 'apt-get update -y'. To approximate: run on an Ubuntu 22.04 (jammy) host/container behind the same Azure mirror pool and repeatedly run 'apt-get update -y' during a mirror sync window; intermittently observe 'Hash Sum mismatch' for jammy-updates/universe or jammy-updates/main Packages.gz.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'Debian Packages' job - this is a transient upstream mirror desync and typically succeeds on retry.

In .github/workflows/job_debian_packages.yml, add 'apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*' before 'apt-get update -y', or add a short retry loop (e.g. 3 attempts with backoff) around the 'apt-get update -y' calls to absorb transient mirror hash mismatches.

Consider passing 'Acquire::http::Pipeline-Depth=0' or switching to a pinned/stable mirror (e.g. a regional official mirror instead of the dynamic azure.archive.ubuntu.com CDN) to reduce mirror-consistency races.
No source code changes are required; this is unrelated to the merged PR (#38934).
prevention_strategies: Wrap 'apt-get update' invocations in CI with a small retry-with-backoff wrapper script shared across workflows (e.g. a composite action 'apt-get-update-retry') so transient mirror Hash Sum mismatches are absorbed automatically instead of failing the whole job. Monitor recurrence via this pattern database; if count grows significantly, consider switching to a vendored/mirrored apt cache for CI runners.
historical_context: No prior investigation in the post-commit database matches this exact signature (Ubuntu apt mirror Hash Sum mismatch). Related but distinct network-flake patterns already tracked include DNS resolution failures during checkout/fetch (eeae3ce3f5218e80), getaddrinfo failures during artifact upload (d877f2bb57b833d0, b6957c2b9e09de1c), and HTTP 503/429/504 failures against npm/HuggingFace/GitHub during dependency installs (09126916fe54469f, 4dd69b5f0be10a15, 8788a3eff93ab889) - all upstream-service transient-network issues, consistent with this being another instance of the broader 'flaky external network dependency in CI' category rather than a new code regression.
